subject: MAP: security intake & DPA retention carveouts — next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alden Harris <alden.harris@pelotonbank.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@pelotonbank.com>

Subject: MAP: security intake & DPA retention carveouts — next steps

Hi Alden / Maya —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our sync, I’m sending a draft mutual action plan (attached) that lays out the security/compliance gates we’ll need to clear during evaluation and before production: SOC 2 attestation, SIG/CAIQ questionnaire completion, DPA redline resolution, and explicit data retention/residency commitments. Key asks up-front:

- Confirm SOC 2 scope required for acceptance (system + common criteria vs. full plus).
- Confirm whether Peloton requires SIG/CAIQ completion or a subset of the questionnaire.
- Confirm retention window you expect for logs and exported data (your note indicated 3 years; we want to clarify which data classes that applies to).
- Please review the DPA redline column in the attached DPA_redlines_peloton.docx and mark any must-haves.

Proposed MAP milestones (high-level):
1) Security intake & evidence exchange (week 1–2) — SOC 2 attestation + SIG kickoff.
2) DPA negotiation & legal review (week 2–3) — target redline resolution.
3) Acceptance testing & retention confirmation (week 3–4).

If these look reasonable I’ll tie dates to each milestone and loop in our legal and security teams for the DPA redline sprint. I attached MAP_v1.xlsx with an editable milestone table and the DPA template.

Next step: can you confirm SOC 2 scope and whether the 3-year retention is required for all data classes or only audit logs / transaction records? Also, are there any internal approvers we should loop into the MAP (beyond legal@pelotonbank.com)?

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee

soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Alden Harris <alden.harris@pelotonbank.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: security intake & DPA retention carveouts — next steps

Soojin —

Thanks for the plan. We reviewed and attached a first-pass DPA with our redlines (DPA_redlines_peloton.docx). High level: we do require a 3-year retention for transaction logs and for exported reporting data used by our compliance team. For ephemeral request-level logs (debug traces) we’d accept a shorter window (90 days).

A couple of clarifying points from our side:
- SOC 2: we prefer a Type II with the security and availability criteria in scope.
- SIG/CAIQ: our security team asks that you complete the full questionnaire; we’ll accept a staggered completion but critical items (encryption at rest, KMS controls, access reviews) should be answered in week 1.

I’ve CC’d legal to review the DPA redlines formally. Please let us know if Redwood can meet the 3-year retention for the specified categories or if you need an exception carveout for certain data classes.

Best,
Alden Harris
Director, Vendor Risk — Peloton Bank
Alden.Harris@pelotonbank.com

Attachment: DPA_redlines_peloton.docx (Peloton redlines)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: security intake & DPA retention carveouts — next steps

Team —

Forwarding Alden’s note (excerpt below) and our initial read on feasibility.

> "we do require a 3-year retention for transaction logs and for exported reporting data used by our compliance team. For ephemeral request-level logs (debug traces) we’d accept a shorter window (90 days)."

Quick take: 
- SOC 2 Type II (security + availability) — we can provide our 2026 attestation (attached SOC2_Attestation_2026.pdf) and coordinate a short evidence sprint to surface controls mapping to Peloton’s acceptance criteria.
- Retention: 3 years for transaction logs and exported reporting can be accommodated with a two-tier model: 1 year hot (fast access, standard retention) + 2 years cold archival (encrypted at rest, slower retrieval, storage in designated region). This reduces live storage costs and aligns with our retention tooling.
- Residency: if Peloton requires EU residency for archived data we can put cold backups into EU GCP buckets (adds a small configuration/time overhead).

Recommend proposing the compromise to Alden with a clear operational note about retrieval SLA for cold archives (we suggest 48–72 hours). Also recommend documenting the exception flow for PII categories that may require different handling.

I’ll prep a short one-page note for legal describing the two-tier retention + retrieval SLA.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2_Attestation_2026.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alden Harris <alden.harris@pelotonbank.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@pelotonbank.com>, legal@pelotonbank.com
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: security intake & DPA retention carveouts — next steps

Alden / Maya / Peloton legal —

Thanks for the redlines. We propose the following DPA language to capture the agreed retention compromise (suggested insertion):

"Data Retention: Redwood will retain transaction logs and exported reporting data for a maximum of three (3) years. Retention will be implemented as a two-tier policy: one (1) year of hot storage with standard access SLA and two (2) years of cold encrypted archival with a maximum retrieval SLA of seventy-two (72) hours. Exported reporting data will be stored in the region requested by Peloton where applicable."

If Peloton accepts, we’ll add the clause to the working DPA and send a DocuSign packet. I’ve also updated MAP_v1.xlsx with dates tied to the acceptance gates: target DPA signature by 2027-06-30, SIG questionnaire completion by 2027-06-25, and MAP acceptance gate on 2027-07-02 (engineering & security sign-off).

Link to proposed packet: https://docusign.example.com/packet/98765
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/54321

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Alden Harris <alden.harris@pelotonbank.com>

Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@pelotonbank.com>, legal@pelotonbank.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: security intake & DPA retention carveouts — next steps

Karthik / team —

Appreciate the suggested language — that read looks good for the most part. One outstanding ask from compliance: we need an exception process for categories containing sensitive PII (national IDs, full account numbers). For those, Peloton’s policy requires either (a) a shorter retention window plus redaction on export, or (b) a contractual carveout that mandates additional safeguards and a named approver.

Can we add a short paragraph to the DPA that describes the exception workflow (routing to Peloton vendor risk with a 10-business-day review SLA)? If possible, we’d like to finalize legal language in the coming week and schedule a short call (30 min) to walk through the final packet.

Happy to take a slot Thursday or Friday next week.

Best,
Alden

Team / Peloton —

Summary & agreed next steps (per thread):

1) SOC 2: Redwood provided SOC2_Attestation_2026.pdf and will schedule a 3-day evidence sprint for mapped controls. Target: evidence sprint week of 2027-06-28.
2) SIG/CAIQ: Redwood will complete the SIG questionnaire; priority controls (encryption, KMS, access reviews) will be answered by 2027-06-18, full questionnaire by 2027-06-25.
3) DPA & retention: Agreed two-tier retention for transaction logs/exported reporting (1 year hot + 2 years cold archive with 72-hour retrieval SLA). Peloton requested an exception workflow for sensitive PII categories; Karthik to add exception paragraph and routing to vendor risk with a 10-business-day review SLA. Target DPA signature via DocuSign: 2027-06-30.
4) Acceptance gates: internal engineering/security sign-off targeted 2027-07-02; go/no-go to production to be confirmed after sign-off.

Action items:
- Karthik: insert exception workflow language into the DPA and circulate updated packet for DocuSign (due 2027-06-25).
- Irene: prepare a one-page operational note outlining cold-archive retrieval SLAs and EU residency option (due 2027-06-18).
- Soojin: schedule a 30-minute legal walk-through call for 2027-06-24 (propose 10:00a PT).

Thanks everyone — I’ll send calendar invites and update MAP_v1.xlsx with the confirmed dates and owners once the DPA text is finalized.

Soojin
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
